**Chapter 1: Transmigrated as the Female Lead of a Trashy CEO Romance**

I woke up on a bed bigger than my entire studio apartment.

Above me hung a crystal chandelier. To my left, floor-to-ceiling windows framed the most expensive skyline in the city. To my right, a smart speaker recited today’s weather and the Pei Corporation’s stock price in a gentle female voice.

Wait. Pei Corporation?

I shot up. A sharp pain stabbed the back of my skull, and a flood of memories that weren’t mine crashed into my brain.

Su Nian. Twenty-four. Executive secretary at Pei Corporation. Last month, she secretly married Pei Yanzhou. According to the original plot, in Chapter 27 she’d get slapped by Pei Yanzhou at the company gala because of a setup orchestrated by the sanctimonious white lotus supporting character. Chapter 89, she’d find out she was pregnant. Chapter 247, she’d run off with the bun in the oven. Chapter 598, he’d chase her down. Chapter 801, the grand finale—the prince and princess living happily and filthily ever after.

Thing is, I’m not Su Nian.

Yesterday, I was still in my rented hole, slurping instant noodles and hate-reading this dumpster fire of an Alpha CEO novel. I stayed up until 3 a.m. roasting the author for padding the word count. Then—poof—I transmigrated inside.

*Ding— Congratulations, Host. You have bound the Dominant CEO Capture System. Main mission: capture Pei Yanzhou’s heart and earn a five-star rating. Current Favorability: -50.*

A translucent blue panel materialized before my eyes, the text rendered in tidy Song typeface.

I took a deep breath.

Alright. Fine. So I transmigrated and got a system. This is the legendary golden finger?

“System,” I thought, “what does -50 Favorability actually mean?”

“Friendly reminder: a -50 Favorability rating means the target finds your mere presence annoying. Host is advised to increase Favorability as soon as possible. Otherwise, the ‘Alpha CEO Slaps the Female Lead’ event will trigger in Chapter 27.”

...

I replayed the Chapter 27 plot in my head. Pei Yanzhou mistakenly believed Su Nian had framed his saintly childhood sweetheart, Lin Wanqing. He slapped Su Nian across the face in front of three hundred people at the Pei Corporation annual gala. Su Nian ran out of the banquet hall in tears, then came back, decided she still wasn’t good enough, and resolved to love him even harder.

Reading that chapter, I got so pissed I nearly hurled my phone at the wall. Now I’m supposed to take that slap in person?

Not happening. Absolutely not.

I threw off the covers and got out of bed. This penthouse was one of Pei Yanzhou’s properties. Su Nian lived here after their secret marriage, but Pei Yanzhou almost never came home. In the novel’s words, “This was nothing more than a gilded cage where he could imprison her.”

Pfft. A cage? This incredible apartment?

I walked into the walk-in closet and pulled open the doors. Hermès. Chanel. Dior. All neatly arrayed, every piece charged to Pei Yanzhou’s black card. The shoe shelves were crammed with red-bottomed heels.

In the novel, Su Nian never wore any of it. She didn’t think she “deserved” them. Every day, she dressed in a white blouse and black skirt like a bank teller.

I picked out a red dress, slipped it on, and checked the mirror.

Not bad. Su Nian’s face really was a knockout. No wonder the novel described her as “so beautiful Pei Yanzhou couldn’t tear his eyes away, though he’d die before admitting it.”

“System, any change in Favorability?”

“Current Favorability: -50. Host has yet to interact with the capture target.”

Fine. No rush. The most important thing right now wasn’t chasing after that stone-faced Alpha CEO. It was stacking my chips before the Chapter 27 plot could trigger.

I picked up my phone and checked Su Nian’s bank account. Six figures. Then I scrolled through her WeChat messages with Pei Yanzhou. The most recent one was from seven days ago: *Working late. Not coming home.*

Scrolling up, the chat history basically went:

Su Nian: *Honey, are you coming home for dinner tonight? I made your favorite braised pork ribs.*
Pei Yanzhou: *In a meeting.*
Su Nian: *Honey, the weather’s getting cold. I left a coat for you at the company front desk.*
Pei Yanzhou: *Mm.*
Su Nian: *Honey, I had my prenatal checkup today—*
Pei Yanzhou: *Busy.*

Hold up.

Prenatal checkup?

I swiped back to that message. Sent three days ago.

Su Nian had peed on a stick, gotten two lines, and messaged Pei Yanzhou. And then—nothing. He hadn’t even sent back a single punctuation mark.

This man.

I tossed the phone onto the bed, walked to the floor-to-ceiling windows, and looked out at the thousand lights of the city below.

The original Su Nian would have cried. She’d have cried alone all night, shown up the next morning with dark circles and a homemade breakfast for Pei Yanzhou, pretending nothing had happened.

But not me.

I transmigrated here from the life of a corporate drone grinding out the 996. In my world, working overtime past midnight was the norm, and instant noodles were a survival skill. A man’s cold silence? That was the prelude to a layoff notice. Su Nian’s problem was she thought of herself as the heroine of a melodramatic soap opera. I’m not her. I’m here to be the queen.

Alpha CEO? Capturing his heart? Favorability?

Give me a break.

I was going to make Pei Yanzhou, that human ATM on legs, learn the true meaning of “paternity privilege.”

*His worth depends on the bun in my oven.*

**Chapter 2: President Pei, Keep Your Distance**

The first time Pei Yanzhou actually saw Su Nian was at the Pei Group quarterly meeting.

Correction—it was the moment she walked into the conference room.

She wasn't wearing her usual white blouse and black skirt. Today, it was a burgundy pencil dress with a matching blazer, seven-inch heels, hair down in loose waves instead of the low ponytail. And her lips were a bold red.

The room went silent for two seconds.

The senior executives stared at Su Nian like she'd grown a second head. The quiet, invisible secretary who normally blended into the furniture looked like a completely different person.

"Good morning, everyone." Su Nian set her coffee on the table, pulled out her chair, and opened her laptop.

Pei Yanzhou frowned.

He noticed. Of course he did. But he would never show it. He was Pei Yanzhou—legend of the business world, worth over a hundred billion by twenty-seven, a man who treated women with a firm "nice-to-have, can-take-or-leave" attitude. No way he'd admit his gaze had lingered on her for that extra half-second.

"Let's begin." Pei Yanzhou's voice was flat.

The marketing director cleared his throat and pulled up a PowerPoint. "President Pei, overseas business grew 20% this quarter, but our competitors are pushing hard in Southeast Asia. We—"

Su Nian raised her hand.

"Actually," she said, "I have a few thoughts."

Every pair of eyes snapped to her.

Su Nian stood up, walked to the projection screen, and pointed the laser at a number. "The Southeast Asia growth rate looks good, but profit margin is only 3.5%. Competitors are expanding, sure, but they're burning investor cash—every market they win, they lose money. Our strategy should be to dig deeper in North America. Last quarter, paying users in the US grew 18%. My suggestion: play defense in Southeast Asia and pour all resources into North America."

The room went silent again.

This time, Pei Yanzhou held his gaze on her for a full three seconds.

Not because of her dress. Not because of her shoes. Because every single word she said was right.

Su Nian sat back down, took a sip of her coffee, and wore an expression as innocent as a cat that had just stolen a fish.

Pei Yanzhou looked away and said one thing to the marketing director: "Do what Su said."

After the meeting, Su Nian walked out with her laptop. The hallway was empty. Just as she reached for the elevator, a hand pressed on her shoulder.

Pei Yanzhou.

"Who are you?"

Her heart skipped a beat. What did he mean? Had he figured her out?

But his next words relaxed her. "You never speak up."

"And I never wear red dresses." Su Nian tilted her head, a smile playing on her lips. "People change, President Pei."

She emphasized "President Pei" just enough to make it sting.

Pei Yanzhou narrowed his eyes. He didn't like things slipping out of his control. Su Nian—that quiet, yes-woman who never contradicted him—had done nothing but defy his expectations today.

"Come home tonight," he said.

"Which home?" Su Nian asked.

He froze. She had never questioned him. When he said "come home," she was supposed to obediently go back, cook dinner, and wait. That was their understanding—no, not an understanding, it was his command.

"You know which home," he said, his voice turning colder.

Su Nian smiled.

She leaned in close to his ear and lowered her voice: "President Pei, you don't even remember where I live, and you have the nerve to say 'come home'?"

With that, she reached over and pressed the elevator button. The doors slid open. She stepped inside, turned around, and gave him a sunny smile.

"See you tomorrow, President Pei. Oh, and—"

Just as the doors were about to close, her voice drifted through the gap:

"Working late tonight. Not coming back."

The second the doors sealed, Su Nian slumped against the wall and exhaled.

"System, how's it looking?"

*Ding—Favorability update: -30. Congratulations, Host. The target's attitude toward you has upgraded from 'can't stand seeing you' to 'what the hell is up with this person today.'*

"...That counts as progress?"

*It does. Twenty-point increase. Beginner reward unlocked: Pei Group Organizational Chart.*

A mind map of the company structure appeared in her head—down to each department head, their reporting lines, the power struggles within the inner circle, and even which VP was keeping a mistress on the side.

"..." Su Nian studied the chart and slowly broke into a grin.

So that was how it worked. The system wasn't about making her suck up to Pei Yanzhou. It was giving her the tools to play the game.

She walked into the parking garage and pulled out Su Nian's keys. A Porsche Panamera, Pei Yanzhou's birthday gift to her last year. Su Nian had never driven it, claiming "I don't know how to drive such an expensive car."

See, that was Su Nian's problem. Give her a fighter jet and she'd use it as a clothesline.

Su Nian started the engine and punched an address into the navigation—the office of Yaoxing Group, Pei Group's archrival.

She wasn't going to defect. She was going to negotiate.

In the original novel, the CEO of Yaoxing Group, Chu Huai, was the second male lead—a gentle soul, always there for Su Nian when trouble hit, a textbook sweet backup. He'd fallen for her at first sight, but Su Nian only ever loved Pei Yanzhou. In the end, Chu Huai walked away in the shadows.

When I read the original novel, I always thought Su Nian was the worst calculator in the world. An Alpha CEO who slaps you and a guardian angel sweetheart—you pick the guy who hits you? What are you, a masochist?

But I wasn't going to hand out a friend-zone card to Chu Huai either. I just needed a contingency plan.

If the slap in Chapter 27 was inevitable, then I needed an ace by that day—something that made Pei Yanzhou think twice before touching me.

Something like an exclusive cooperation agreement with Yaoxing Group.

The Panamera pulled out of the garage and merged into city traffic. The stereo switched on to an old song that Su Nian had queued up before.

*"I don't want to be a caged bird, watching the sky without freedom..."*

Su Nian turned it off.

*Su Nian, your song's over. Let me sing a different one.*

Chu Huai set down his coffee cup and studied the woman sitting across from him.

He'd known Su Nian for three years. Or rather, he'd watched her from afar for three years—always on the periphery of Pei Yanzhou. That woman who forever kept her head down, spoke as softly as a mosquito, and bit her lip nervously whenever Pei Yanzhou was around. Today she wore a sharp black jumpsuit, crossed her legs, and spoke with the easygoing tone of someone chatting with an old friend at a tea house.

"Mr. Chu, I'll get straight to the point." Su Nian slid a document across the table. "Yaoxing is doing overseas short dramas. Pei Group handles overseas web novel distribution. The two businesses don't conflict—they complement each other. I propose we sign an exclusive channel cooperation agreement: Yaoxing's short dramas go through Pei Group's platform exclusively for overseas distribution, and Pei Group gives Yaoxing a five-percentage-point cut on the split."

Chu Huai picked up the file and flipped through it, his expression shifting from polite to serious.

"Secretary Su, this proposal... does CEO Pei know about it?"

"No," Su Nian said, taking a sip of her coffee. "But in this morning's meeting, he said, 'Handle overseas operations as Secretary Su sees fit.' So I'm taking that as authorization."

Chu Huai laughed. He had one of those warm laughs that made you feel at ease—completely the opposite of Pei Yanzhou, whose laugh made you want to run.

"Aren't you afraid he'll be angry when he finds out?"

"Mr. Chu," Su Nian set down her cup, "the biggest thing I've learned in life is that anger works better than tears. Let him be mad. I'll get the job done."

Chu Huai looked into Su Nian's eyes and was silent for a few seconds.

"Do you like him?" he asked suddenly.

The question caught Su Nian off guard.

Not because she didn't know how to answer. But because in the original story, Chu Huai had asked, "Is he good to you?" And Su Nian had replied, "He just loves me in his own way." Then Chu Huai would fall silent and drink alone all night.

But today's Su Nian had changed the script. "He's good to me" had become "Do you like him?" And Chu Huai had changed too.

"No," Su Nian said.

Chu Huai raised an eyebrow.

"Not only that," Su Nian continued, "I'm planning to make him 'Father Rises by Son.'"

Chu Huai nearly spat out his coffee.

"Wait," he wiped his mouth, "by 'Father Rises by Son,' do you mean what I think you mean?"

"Yes. I'm pregnant. Pei Yanzhou doesn't know yet. I'm putting together a plan to get him to proactively invest in Yaoxing during my pregnancy. I need your cooperation."

Chu Huai leaned back in his seat, his expression complicated.

"Su Nian, you're not the Su Nian I used to know."

"So which version do you like better?"

Chu Huai didn't answer immediately. He looked at Su Nian—not at her face, not at her clothes, but at her eyes. Those eyes held a light he'd never seen before. Like a bird that had just flown out of its cage, still getting used to the direction of the wind.

"This version," Chu Huai said. "I like this version."

*Ding—detected high-quality backup affection +10. Friendly reminder: Host has entered the 'two-timing' plot branch. Current affection: Pei Yanzhou -30, Chu Huai +60.*

Su Nian mentally rolled her eyes at the system.

"I'm not two-timing," she corrected inwardly. "One boat is Pei Yanzhou's. The other is my own."

For the next forty minutes, Su Nian and Chu Huai hammered out the cooperation framework. Yaoxing would provide short drama content, Pei Group would handle overseas distribution channels, and they renegotiated the revenue split—Chu Huai got two percentage points lower than expected but secured an exclusivity commitment.

"One last question." Chu Huai stood to see her out. "Are you doing this sincerely, or just to piss off Pei Yanzhou?"

Su Nian thought about it. "Fifty-fifty. Half sincere, half spite."

Chu Huai laughed out loud. "Next time you come see me, I hope the ratio shifts."

"To what?"

"Sixty-forty. Sixty percent sincere."

Su Nian didn't answer. She just waved and stepped into the elevator.

Back in her Panamera, she rested her head on the steering wheel, closed her eyes, and took a deep breath.

Nausea.

Not because of Chu Huai. Morning sickness.

She'd almost thrown up that coffee right there in Chu Huai's office. She held it together for forty minutes without changing expression—a career-best acting performance.

"System, is there any way to suppress the morning sickness?"

*Available for exchange: Pregnancy BUFF: Morning Sickness Time Shift Card. Exchange? Requires 10 affection points.*

"...Whose points?"

*Pei Yanzhou.*

"Deduct. Whatever."

*Ding—affection update: Pei Yanzhou -40. Card exchanged. Effect: Morning sickness concentrated between 3:00 AM and 4:00 AM daily; no effect the rest of the day.*

3 AM. Great. She was already awake then. Ever since she'd been transported into this body, she woke up at three every morning—not because of her biological clock, but because of anger. Anger at a man she'd never met. Anger at the setting of this world. Anger that the female lead of some cliché web novel had to wait until chapter 801 to be happy.

3 AM. She wouldn't sleep. She'd review every move she made today, plan every path for tomorrow.

Her phone rang.

Pei Yanzhou.

Su Nian glanced at the screen and picked up.

"Where are you?" His voice was laced with fury.

"In the car."

"Who told you to go see Chu Huai?"

Su Nian smiled. News traveled fast.

"CEO Pei," she said, her voice dripping honey, "you said it yourself this morning—handle overseas operations as I see fit. Mr. Chu of Yaoxing is the biggest short drama content provider overseas. I was following your instructions."

A two-second silence on the other end.

"Come home. Now." Pei Yanzhou said.

"Which home?"

"Su Nian—"

*Beep—*

Su Nian hung up.

She switched her phone to airplane mode, started the engine, and headed east. Not back to that penthouse apartment. She was going to see a house. A house that belonged to her alone. Using Su Nian's own savings—a six-figure deposit, enough for a down payment on a small two-bedroom in the development zone.

In the original novel, Su Nian never touched that money. She always felt she "didn't deserve it." Her money was Pei Yanzhou's money, her person was Pei Yanzhou's person, her life was a cliché web novel revolving around Pei Yanzhou.

Su Nian, you held all the best cards. Beauty. Education. High salary. A man. A system. And the ultimate trump card in your belly.

But you did nothing. Just waited there for a slap.

I'll play for you.

I'll play every card and flip that -50 affection score into the most brilliant business legend this city has ever seen.

You want the father to rise by the son? Fine.

Let's see how long this iceberg called Pei Yanzhou can hold out.

(Chapters 1-3 End)
